problem: Existing VLN pre-training methods (PREVALENT, HAMT, AirBert, DUET, etc.) use discrete panoramas as visual input. The model must implicitly relate incomplete observations within a view and duplicate observations across views, which weakens spatial reasoning. Map-based navigation has not been combined with large-scale VLN pre-training. Purely metric maps are too expensive to hold long-horizon dependencies, and purely topological maps compress each node into one vector, losing fine-grained local layout.
motivation: Instructions such as 'the second bedroom opposite to the bookcase' require knowing whether duplicate views show the same object or several instances. Projecting views into a unified bird's-eye map removes duplicates and aggregates partial views. Classic topo-metric SLAM suggests the fix: a small local metric map for short-term reasoning plus a global topological graph for long-term planning and backtracking. The paper makes this hybrid map learnable and multimodal, and pre-trains on it.
key_idea: Pre-train a cross-modal transformer on a hybrid map built from expert paths: a global topological graph (node-level long-term planning) and a local egocentric 21x21 grid of ground-projected CLIP features (cell-level short-term reasoning). Proxy tasks are MLM, hybrid action prediction and masked semantic imagination; the two branches' action scores are fused with a gate that depends on the agent state.
insight: The main gain comes from pairing a local metric map with a topological graph. In the Table 'Comparison of map variants' (R2R val-unseen): topo-only gets 70.25 SR / 61.29 SPL, metric-only gets about 60.9 SR (high TL, poor long-term exploration), and the hybrid gets 74.88 SR / 63.60 SPL. Simply fusing depth features into topo nodes gives nothing (70.03 SR), so the benefit comes from explicit spatial layout, not from depth as an input. Pre-training matters most: training from scratch gives 60.24 SR / 48.29 SPL, versus 73.52 SR with MLM only. HSAP mainly improves efficiency (+2.90 SPL), and MSI (predicting semantics of masked cells) adds +0.85 SR. The metric map is built in feature space from coarse 14x14 depth, so RedNet-estimated depth performs almost the same as sensed depth (74.67 vs 74.88 SR). Further findings: 1st-order integration of neighbouring views (κ=1) is enough; enlarging the map to 31x31 brings no gain (SR 74.84 vs 74.88) at about 2x FLOPs (32.7G vs 15.2G); CLIP grid features beat ImageNet ViT (74.88 vs 74.03 SR).
method: Image processing: ViT-B/16-CLIP extracts per-view feature vectors (for topo nodes) and 14x14 grid features (for the metric map); depth is downsized to the same 14x14 scale.

Topological mapping: a graph of visited, current and ghost nodes with Euclidean-distance edges. Visited/current nodes take the average of pano-encoder (2-layer transformer, as in HAMT) view embeddings; ghost nodes accumulate the embeddings of the views that observed them. The global action space is all observed nodes.

Local metric mapping: an egocentric 21x21 grid (0.5 m cells, 10.5 m span). Grid features from nodes within κ=1 topological order are ground-projected with depth and pose, and collisions within a cell are average-pooled. Local action space = the current node plus adjacent nodes, mapped node→cell.

Dual cross-modal encoders (LXMERT-style, initialized from LXMERT; RoBERTa for RxR): a 9-layer text encoder, a 4-layer long-term topo encoder with graph-aware self-attention (from DUET) over nodes plus a 'stop' node, and a 4-layer short-term metric encoder over cells. Cells carry an egocentric polar position embedding [cos θ, sin θ, dist] and a navigability embedding.

Hybrid action fusion: separate FFNs score nodes and the converted local cells. Scores are fused as δ·s^G + (1−δ)·s^M, where δ = sigmoid(FFN([stop node; center cell])); visited nodes are masked out. Distant (long-term) targets are reached via Dijkstra shortest path on the topo map.

Pre-training tasks on offline maps from chunked expert paths: MLM (15% masking; text outputs of both branches are summed), HSAP (single-step action cross-entropy on fused scores), and MSI (mask 15% of cells and predict 40-class Matterport3D semantics with multi-label BCE). Sampling ratio is 5:5:1. REVERIE instead uses MLM:HSAP:MRC:OG = 1:1:1:1, with objects fed into the metric branch.

Fine-tuning: online map construction with alternating teacher-forcing and student-forcing, supervised by DUET-style pseudo labels (shortest-path labels for R2R/R2R-CE/REVERIE, nDTW-fidelity labels for RxR), with λ=0.2 (0.8 for RxR). For R2R-CE, a CWP waypoint predictor produces the nodes, organized as a topo map in the style of ETPNav.

setting.backbone: LXMERT-initialized cross-modal transformer (9-layer text encoder, two 4-layer map encoders, hidden 768; RoBERTa init for multilingual RxR) on frozen ViT-B/16-CLIP visual features; trained/fine-tuned
setting.training_data: Per-dataset training splits plus synthetic instructions: PREVALENT augmentation for R2R/R2R-CE, RxR-Marky (Marky-mT5) for RxR, REVERIE-Spk for REVERIE. MSI labels come from Matterport3D 40-class semantics. Pre-training: 100k iters, batch 64; fine-tuning: 40k iters, batch 16 (4x A100).
setting.observation: panoramic RGB-D + agent pose (depth can be RedNet-estimated from RGB); REVERIE additionally uses candidate object annotations
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (select any observed ghost node or stop; multi-hop moves via Dijkstra on the topo map); R2R-CE: predicted waypoints (CWP) executed with low-level actions
setting.privileged: GT agent pose provided to simplify mapping; sensed (GT) depth by default (estimated depth ablated); nav-graph candidate viewpoints in discrete VLN; GT semantics only for pre-training labels

results:
BEVBert sets state-of-the-art on four benchmarks:
- R2R: 75 SR / 64 SPL on val-unseen and 73 SR / 62 SPL on test-unseen, beating DUET by +4 SR / +3 SPL on test. Only the 3-agent EnvEdit ensemble has higher SPL (64).
- R2R-CE: 59 SR / 50 SPL on test-unseen, versus ETPNav's 55 / 48.
- RxR test-unseen: 64.4 SR / 65.4 nDTW / 54.2 SDTW, beating the EnvEdit ensemble (60.4 / 64.6 / 51.8).
- REVERIE: 51.78 SR / 34.71 RGS on val-unseen (+4.80 SR over DUET), but only a marginal gain on test-unseen (52.81 vs 52.51 SR).
limitations: Relies on known agent pose and depth to build the metric map (estimated depth works nearly as well on R2R, but pose is given). In discrete VLN it also relies on nav-graph candidates.

Metric map cost grows roughly quadratically with map scale, so the map is limited to a small local window. Fine-tuning memory grows with trajectory length, so the paper cuts text-branch attention in the map encoders.
Gains on REVERIE test-unseen are marginal (+0.3 SR over DUET), and the MSI task is dropped on REVERIE. Performance remains far below humans (e.g., RxR test 64.4 vs 93.9 SR).
